issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: squash orzo, and a rye loaf for the weekend
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-squash-orzo-and-a-rye-loaf-for-the-weekend

Morning {first},

The squash at the market has been absurdly cheap this week, so it's in the weeknight recipe. The weekend project is a rye loaf, because it's finally cool enough to want the oven on all afternoon.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Squash, sage and brown butter orzo
Serves 2, 35 minutes

You'll need:
- half a butternut squash, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
- 200g orzo
- 40g butter
- a small bunch of sage
- 1 garlic clove
- a lemon
- parmesan or a hard cheese, to grate

1. Roast the squash at 200C with oil and salt for 25 minutes, until the edges catch.
2. Meanwhile, cook the orzo in salted water for 8 minutes. Keep a mug of the water.
3. Melt the butter in a wide pan until it smells of hazelnuts. Add the sage leaves and the sliced garlic for a minute.
4. Tip in the orzo, the squash, a splash of the water and a squeeze of lemon. Stir until glossy, then grate over the cheese.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/squash-sage-and-brown-butter-orzo

THIS WEEKEND

A caraway rye loaf
One 900g loaf, about 5 hours, mostly waiting
This is a 50% rye, so it's sticky but still forgiving. Mix 250g rye flour, 250g strong white, 8g salt, 7g instant yeast, 2 teaspoons caraway and 380ml warm water. It won't knead like a white dough: just work it with a wet hand for five minutes. Prove for two hours, shape, prove an hour more in a tin, and bake at 220C for 45 minutes. Wait until tomorrow to slice it. I know.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/a-caraway-rye-loaf

FROM THE LARDER

Brown butter keeps in the fridge for a week. Make double and use the rest on Monday's eggs.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

--

issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: chickpea and chard stew, and quick pickles
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-chickpea-and-chard-stew-and-quick-pickles

Morning {first},

This week is about the jar. A stew that tastes better on day two, and pickled onions that'll make everything else you eat this month better.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Chickpea and chard stew
Serves 4, 40 minutes

You'll need:
- 2 tins of chickpeas, with their liquid
- a bunch of chard, stalks and leaves separated
- 1 onion and 3 garlic cloves
- a tin of chopped tomatoes
- 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- a good piece of bread, to serve

1. Soften the onion and the chopped chard stalks in olive oil for 10 minutes.
2. Add the garlic and paprika, then the tomatoes and the chickpeas with their liquid.
3. Simmer for 20 minutes, then stir in the shredded leaves until they wilt.
4. Season well. Serve with bread, and keep half for tomorrow.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/chickpea-and-chard-stew

THIS WEEKEND

Quick pickled red onions
One jar, 15 minutes, ready in an hour
Slice two red onions thinly and pack them into a clean jar. Warm 150ml cider vinegar, 150ml water, 1 tablespoon sugar and 2 teaspoons salt until dissolved, then pour over. Add a few peppercorns and a bay leaf if you have them. They're pink and ready in an hour and keep for three weeks in the fridge.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/quick-pickled-red-onions

FROM THE LARDER

Keep the chickpea water. It whips like egg white, and it thickens soups.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: lemon chicken traybake, and focaccia
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-lemon-chicken-traybake-and-focaccia

Morning {first},

One tray, one dish. The weeknight recipe this week makes almost no washing up, and the weekend one is the focaccia people keep asking me for.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Lemon chicken traybake with potatoes and olives
Serves 2, 50 minutes

You'll need:
- 4 chicken thighs, skin on
- 400g small potatoes, halved
- a lemon, cut into wedges
- a handful of green olives
- a few sprigs of thyme
- olive oil, salt and pepper

1. Heat the oven to 210C.
2. Toss everything in a roasting tin with oil and salt, chicken skin side up.
3. Roast for 45 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the potatoes are golden.
4. Squeeze the roasted lemon over everything before serving.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/lemon-chicken-traybake-with-potatoes-and-olives

THIS WEEKEND

Rosemary focaccia
One tray, about 4 hours
Mix 500g strong white flour, 10g salt, 5g instant yeast and 400ml water into a wet dough. Fold it in the bowl four times over two hours. Pour plenty of oil into a tin, tip in the dough and leave for an hour. Dimple with oiled fingers, scatter rosemary and flaky salt, and bake at 230C for 25 minutes.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/rosemary-focaccia

FROM THE LARDER

Stale focaccia makes the best croutons. Tear, oil, bake at 180C until gold.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

--

issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: sardine spaghetti, and marmalade
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-sardine-spaghetti-and-marmalade

Morning {first},

A store cupboard dinner and a weekend in the kitchen with a lot of oranges. If you don't like sardines, use a tin of tuna and don't tell me.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Spaghetti with sardines, lemon and breadcrumbs
Serves 2, 20 minutes

You'll need:
- 200g spaghetti
- a tin of sardines in olive oil
- a handful of breadcrumbs
- 2 garlic cloves
- a pinch of chilli flakes
- a lemon and some parsley

1. Fry the breadcrumbs in a little of the sardine oil until crisp. Set aside.
2. Cook the spaghetti. Meanwhile, warm the garlic and chilli in the rest of the oil.
3. Add the sardines and break them up with a spoon.
4. Toss in the pasta with a splash of its water, the lemon zest and parsley. Top with the crumbs.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/spaghetti-with-sardines-lemon-and-breadcrumbs

THIS WEEKEND

A small batch of marmalade
About 4 jars, most of a Saturday
Simmer 500g oranges whole in 1.2 litres of water for two hours, until soft. Halve them, scoop the pips into a muslin, and slice the peel as thick or thin as you like. Return everything to the pan with 1kg sugar and boil hard until it reaches setting point, about 20 minutes. Test on a cold saucer: it should wrinkle when pushed.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/a-small-batch-of-marmalade

FROM THE LARDER

Jam jars sterilise in a low oven, 140C for 15 minutes. Fill them while they're still warm.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

--

issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: miso aubergine, and a slow ragu
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-miso-aubergine-and-a-slow-ragu

Morning {first},

Two recipes that are mostly about patience: one for twenty minutes, one for four hours. Both worth it.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Miso-glazed aubergine with rice
Serves 2, 35 minutes

You'll need:
- 2 aubergines, halved lengthways
- 2 tablespoons white miso
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 1 tablespoon rice vinegar
- spring onions and sesame seeds
- rice, to serve

1. Score the cut sides of the aubergines in a crisscross and brush with oil.
2. Roast cut side down at 200C for 20 minutes, until soft.
3. Mix the miso, honey and vinegar. Turn the aubergines over and spread it on.
4. Grill for 5 minutes until bubbling. Serve over rice with the onions and seeds.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/miso-glazed-aubergine-with-rice

THIS WEEKEND

A slow beef ragu
Serves 6, 4 hours
Brown 1kg of beef shin in pieces, in batches. Soften an onion, a carrot and a stick of celery, all finely chopped, then add a glass of red wine, two tins of tomatoes and the beef. Cover and cook on the lowest heat for three to four hours, until the meat falls apart. Shred it with two forks. It freezes well, so make the whole lot.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/a-slow-beef-ragu

FROM THE LARDER

Miso keeps for months in the fridge. A teaspoon in a gravy or a soup does a lot.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

--

issues.subject: Brine & Crumb: green fried rice, and sourdough crackers
issues.text:
BRINE & CRUMB
One weeknight dinner, one weekend project. Saturday {date}

View in your browser: https://brineandcrumb.example/issues/brine-and-crumb-green-fried-rice-and-sourdough-crackers

Morning {first},

This week's theme, if there is one, is leftovers. Yesterday's rice for dinner, and the sourdough discard you've been feeling guilty about for a snack.

THIS WEEKNIGHT

Green fried rice with a fried egg
Serves 2, 15 minutes

You'll need:
- 2 bowls of cold cooked rice
- a big handful of spinach or kale, chopped
- a handful of frozen peas
- 2 spring onions
- 1 tablespoon soy sauce
- 2 eggs

1. Heat a wok or wide pan until very hot, with a little oil.
2. Fry the rice, pressing it against the pan, for 3 minutes.
3. Add the greens, peas and spring onions and toss until the greens wilt.
4. Season with soy. Fry the eggs separately and put one on each bowl.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/green-fried-rice-with-a-fried-egg

THIS WEEKEND

Sourdough discard crackers
Two trays, 1 hour
Mix 200g sourdough discard, 100g plain flour, 50g melted butter and a teaspoon of salt into a dough. Roll it as thin as you can between two sheets of baking paper, brush with water, and scatter with seeds and flaky salt. Score into squares and bake at 180C for 20 to 25 minutes, until crisp all the way through.

Printable recipe: https://brineandcrumb.example/recipes/sourdough-discard-crackers

FROM THE LARDER

Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and kept in the fridge for no more than a day.

Happy cooking,
Hattie

--
